notes:
Need to search first.I couldn't do this research, so there are no commentary notes on Isaiah 51 to give you yet.

My first attempt to open the commentary pages failed because the fetch tool only opens pages that a search has already returned, and I hadn't run any searches. Running the searches would have fixed that, but by then the tool had hit its usage limit for this turn. So I didn't read a single page from Enduring Word, Bible Hub, StudyLight, Precept Austin, the NET Bible notes or any of the other approved sites.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and to give a URL for every point. With nothing read, the only honest result is to leave everything out, so I haven't written any verse notes from memory.

If you ask again in a new message, I'll search first and then read the pages in this order:
1. **Traditional reading:** Enduring Word on Isaiah 51, Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary (on StudyLight or Bible Hub), and Precept Austin.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** searches on the key verses in each tradition's own sources. These are the rock and quarry and Abraham (vv. 1–2), the law and justice going out to the nations (vv. 4–5), the arm of the Lord, Rahab and the dragon (vv. 9–10), "I have put My words in your mouth" (v. 16), and the cup of wrath (vv. 17–23).
3. **Other views:** NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship (for example, Rahab and ancient Near Eastern myth), New Advent, Catholic.com and OCA for Catholic and Orthodox readings, and any pages on these sites about debated popular teaching on these verses.

The notes will be verse by verse, with a URL after each point, and any verse I can't find support for will be left out.
